chapter_name: Bipolar and Related Disorders and Depressive Disorders
chapter_title: Bipolar and Related Disorders and Depressive Disorders

questions.question_text: According to DSM-5 all of the following statements regarding disruptive mood dysregulation disorder are correct except:

options.text: The mood symptoms and temper outbursts present at least two settings, and are present for more than 12 months.
This disorder was categorized under bipolar and related disorders.
The temper outbursts are frequent and the mood between temper outbursts is persistently irritable or angry in nature.
Children with this disorder present with severe recurrent temper outbursts that are inconsistent with developmental level.
Onset of these symptoms has to be before the age of 10 years.

correct_answer.text: This disorder was categorized under bipolar and related disorders.

correct_answers.text: This disorder was categorized under bipolar and related disorders.

questions.explanation: Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder is a brand new diagnosis in DSM-5 under the category of depressive disorders. The intention of adding this diagnosis was to address the concerns about the potential for overdiagnosing of and over-treating for bipolar disorder in children. The disorder refers to a pattern of mood dysregulation, chronic and persistent irritability, and frequent extreme behavioral dyscontrol in children who do not present with typical, classic, distinct episodes of mania or hypomania. In DSM-5 the term 'bipolar disorder' is explicitly reserved for the episodic nature of bipolar manifestations. Studies show that children with chronic irritability are at risk to develop unipolar depression and/or anxiety disorders in adulthood with low rate of conversation to bipolar disorders.

questions.question_text: According to DSM-5 the diagnosis of disruptive mood dysregulation disorder cannot be made prior to which of the following ages:

correct_answer.text: 6-year-old

correct_answers.text: 6-year-old

questions.explanation: Based on DSM-5 the diagnosis of disruptive mood dysregulation disorder should not be made for the first time before age 6 years or after age 18 years. However, by history or observation, the onset of symptoms of temper outbursts and chronic irritable/angry mood has to be before age 10 years.

questions.question_text: Prevalence of major depressive disorder in children is lower (about 2%) than in adolescents (about 4–8%). What is the male to female ratio during childhood?
questions.explanation: Prevalence of major depressive disorder in children is lower (approximately 2%) than in adolescents (approximately 4–8%). The male to female ratio during childhood is 1:1, but 1:2 during adolescence, with increased prevalence by twofold to fourfold after puberty, especially in females.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is the most frequent comorbid diagnosis with major depressive disorder in youth?

correct_answer.text: Anxiety disorders

correct_answers.text: Anxiety disorders

questions.explanation: About 40–90% of youth with depressive disorders have other psychiatric disorders, anxiety disorders being the most frequent comorbid diagnoses, followed by disruptive disorders, ADHD, and, in adolescence, substance-related and addictive disorders. Major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) can co-occur, which is called 'double depression.'

questions.question_text: Based on DSM-5 all of the following statements regarding diagnosing major depressive disorder in youth are correct except:

options.text: Any existing manic or hypomanic episodes will exclude major depressive disorder diagnosis.
A substantial portion of people with bipolar illnesses initially present with a major depressive episode.
In children and adolescents, depressed mood can be irritable mood.
Consider failure to make expected weight gain: referring to significant weight loss when not dieting.
Almost identical DSM-5 criteria are used in diagnosing major depressive disorder in both youth and adults.

correct_answer.text: In children and adolescents, depressed mood can be irritable mood.

correct_answers.text: In children and adolescents, depressed mood can be irritable mood.

questions.explanation: In DSM-5 there is only one set of criteria for major depressive disorder, with only two notes to specify the different manifestations between children/adolescents and adults: (1) in children and adolescents, depressed mood can be irritable mood; (2) in children, consider failure to make expected weight gain: referring to significant weight loss when not dieting. Any existing manic or hypomanic episodes will exclude major depressive disorder diagnosis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding diagnosing persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) are correct except:

options.text: Specifiers include 'with mood-congruent psychotic features' and 'with mood-incongruent psychotic features.'
Depressed mood can be irritable mood.
Four specifiers were added to describe absence or presence of coexisting major depressive episodes.
Early onset is before age 21 and later onset is at age 21 or older.
Duration of symptoms can be longer in children for dysthymic disorder.

correct_answer.text: Duration of symptoms can be longer in children for dysthymic disorder.

correct_answers.text: Duration of symptoms can be longer in children for dysthymic disorder.

questions.explanation: Compared to DSM-IV-TR, a few new specifiers were added in DSM-5 for dysthymic disorder that also got a brand new name: persistent depressive disorder. In children and adolescents, duration can be shorter (must be at least one year) and mood can be irritable.

questions.question_text: Based on DSM-5, which of the following is the key diagnostic difference for cyclothymic disorder in children/adolescents compared to adults?

correct_answer.text: Duration of the symptoms required

correct_answers.text: Duration of the symptoms required

questions.explanation: Similar to persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), duration of the symptoms required for children and adolescents is shorter (one year) compared to for adults (two years) in making a diagnosis of cyclothymic disorder in DSM-5.

questions.question_text: Based on DSM-5 children and adolescents who experience multiple episodes of hypomanic symptoms that do not meet criteria for a hypomanic episode and multiple episodes of depressive symptoms that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode that persist less than 12 months, but have no symptom-free periods longer than two months, should be diagnosed with which of the following diagnoses?

options.text: Other specified bipolar and related disorder

correct_answer.text: Other specified bipolar and related disorder

correct_answers.text: Other specified bipolar and related disorder

questions.explanation: DSM-5 recognizes that many people, especially children and adolescents, experience bipolar-like phenomena that do not meet the criteria for bipolar I, II, or cyclothymic disorder. Other specified bipolar and related disorder was designed for clinicians to communicate the specific reason that the presentation does not meet the criteria for any specific bipolar and related disorder.

questions.question_text: In a large randomized controlled trial (RCT), Treatment of Adolescents with Depression Study (TADS) 2004, which of the following type of psychotherapies showed no difference compared to placebo in treating adolescents with MDD?

correct_answer.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)

correct_answers.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)

questions.explanation: In TADS, combination of CBT and fluoxetine showed the best outcome with a rapid decline in depressive symptoms. However, it did not show a significant difference compared to fluoxetine alone at endpoint. These two treatment groups were better compared to either CBT alone or placebo during acute treatment.

questions.question_text: Based on a meta-analysis of all published and unpublished pharmacological RCTs for MDD in youth (Bridge et al. 2007), which pair of the following numbers most closely reflects the average response rates of SSRI antidepressants compared to placebo?
questions.explanation: Based on a meta-analysis of all published and unpublished pharmacological RCTs for MDD in youth (Bridge et al. 2007), the average response rates from SSRI antidepressants compared to placebo was 61% to 50%, which showed relatively high placebo rates, especially in children compared to adolescents.

questions.question_text: Based on a meta-analysis of all published and unpublished pharmacological RCTs for MDD in youth (Bridge et al. 2007), which pair of the following numbers most closely reflects the 'number needed to treat' compared to the 'number needed to harm'?
questions.explanation: The 'number needed to treat' was 10 and the 'number needed to harm' was 112.

questions.question_text: Supported by retrospective case reports and clinical experience (without prospective randomized controlled trials), electro-convulsive therapy (ECT) can be indicated and considered in treating adolescents with severe mood symptoms—depressive or manic in the context of MDD, psychotic depression, schizoaffective disorder, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and catatonia, especially when the conditions are refractory or resistant to conventional therapies. All of the following are likely neurobiological effects of ECT except:

options.text: Increased dopamine D1 receptor density and second messenger potentiation
Increased muscarinic acetylcholine receptor density in cortex and hippocampus
Increased serotonergic responses mediated by the 5-HT2 receptor

correct_answer.text: Increased muscarinic acetylcholine receptor density in cortex and hippocampus

correct_answers.text: Increased muscarinic acetylcholine receptor density in cortex and hippocampus

questions.explanation: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor density in cortex and hippocampus is decreased, which may be relevant for the cognitive side effects of ECT.

questions.question_text: Based on data from up-to-date clinical trials, which of the following antidepressants showed the largest response rate in treating MDD in children and adolescents?

correct_answer.text: Fluoxetine (Prozac)

correct_answers.text: Fluoxetine (Prozac)

questions.explanation: Based on data from up-to-date clinical trials, fluoxetine (Prozac) showed the largest response rate in treating MDD in children and adolescents compared to other antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medical conditions should be the least considered in the differential diagnosis of major depressive disorder?

correct_answer.text: Hyperthyroidism

correct_answers.text: Hyperthyroidism

questions.explanation: Hypothyroidism (not hyperthyroidism) is more likely to manifest with symptoms similar to those of major depressive disorders. Thus, it should be considered as one of potential medical differentials along with certain cancers, autoimmune diseases, anemia, multiple sclerosis, stroke, and others listed in the question when evaluating major depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales is the least useful as a screening instrument when evaluating youth with possible bipolar disorder?

options.text: Parent-completed versions of the General Behavioral Inventory (P-GBI)

correct_answer.text: Vanderbilt Rating Scale

correct_answers.text: Vanderbilt Rating Scale

questions.explanation: Vanderbilt Rating Scales are more useful in screening youth with possible ADHD, oppositional defiant disorder (ODD), and conduct disorder (CD).

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotics does not have an FDA-approved indication for treating youth with bipolar I disorder?

correct_answer.text: Ziprasidone (Geodon)

correct_answers.text: Ziprasidone (Geodon)

questions.explanation: Ziprasidone (Geodon) does not have any FDA-approved indications for children or adolescents at this time.

questions.question_text: Based on new research findings, regarding treatment of ADHD in children with possible or definite mania, which of the following statements is more accurate?

options.text: Treating ADHD symptoms can start prior to treating mood symptoms.
Outcomes of treatment are the same for youth with bipolar disorders alone compared to youth with bipolar disorder comorbid with ADHD.
Apparent return of worse ADHD symptoms at the end of day has diagnostic implications.
Treating ADHD symptoms is always considered a higher priority than treating mood symptoms.
Typical ADHD medications always should be avoided before stabilizing mood symptoms.

correct_answer.text: Treating ADHD symptoms can start prior to treating mood symptoms.

correct_answers.text: Treating ADHD symptoms can start prior to treating mood symptoms.

questions.explanation: Consensus documents recommended stabilizing mood symptoms first, then treating the comorbid disorder. However, some new data suggested treating ADHD symptoms either with or without first stabilizing mood can be considered for children with ADHD along with possible or definite mania.

questions.question_text: Which of the following agents has an FDA-approved indication for treating bipolar I disorder acute depression in children?

correct_answer.text: Olanzapine/fluoxetine (Symbyax)

correct_answers.text: Olanzapine/fluoxetine (Symbyax)

questions.explanation: Olanzapine/fluoxetine (Symbyax) is the only medication that so far has an FDA-approved indication for treating acute depression in children with bipolar disorder (age 10 to 17).

questions.question_text: Studies showed rates of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) induced 'switching' are higher in children than in adolescents and adults. What is the average rate of such risk?
questions.explanation: The average rate of switching by SSRIs is 10%. Because it is not uncommon that the first mood episode of children/adolescents with bipolar disorder is a depressive episode, it is important to inquire for a family history of bipolar disorder and for any history indicative of bipolarity.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements about the epidemiology of depressive disorders in children and adolescents are accurate except:

options.text: Point prevalence of depressive disorder is lower in prepubertal children than in adolescents.
Pre-pubertal onset depressive disorder is more likely to lead to recurrent episodes in adulthood.
Pre-pubertal depressive disorder shares similar risk factors and course with conduct disorder.
Early onset of puberty is a risk factor for girls to develop depression.
In adolescents the rate of depressive disorders in females is three times more than in males.

correct_answer.text: Pre-pubertal onset depressive disorder is more likely to lead to recurrent episodes in adulthood.

correct_answers.text: Pre-pubertal onset depressive disorder is more likely to lead to recurrent episodes in adulthood.

questions.explanation: Adolescent-onset depression is more likely to lead to recurrent episodes in adulthood. The point prevalence of depressive disorder is lower in children (1–2%) than in adolescents (3–8%). Female predominance in depression emerges after onset of puberty, possibly due to hormonal changes, higher comorbid anxiety, and increased interpersonal conflicts in females.

questions.question_text: Based on meta-analysis of pediatric bipolar disorder, which of the following symptoms is the least frequent?

correct_answer.text: Hypersexuality

correct_answers.text: Hypersexuality

questions.explanation: Based on a meta-analysis of studies of pediatric bipolar disorder, the frequency of the symptoms follows the following order (from the most frequent to the least frequent): increased energy, distractibility, pressured speech, irritability, grandiosity, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, euphoria/elation, poor judgment, flight of ideas, and hypersexuality.

questions.question_text: Based on comparative studies on the phenomenology of bipolar disorder and ADHD in youth, which of the following symptoms was found significantly more frequently in bipolar disorder?

correct_answer.text: None of the above

correct_answers.text: None of the above

questions.explanation: With significant overlap of symptoms shared between bipolar disorder and other common psychiatric conditions, especially ADHD, none of the symptoms listed in the question is specific to mania.

questions.question_text: In the study 'Pediatric bipolar spectrum disorder and ADHD: comparison and comorbidity in the LAMS clinical sample' (L. E. Arnold et al. 2011) the authors proposed four hypotheses, two of which were supported, one partially supported, and one rejected. All of the following statements are consistent with their results except:

options.text: Parent ratings of ADHD symptoms were higher for comorbid ADHD+BPSD than for ADHD or BPSD alone.
Rates of other comorbid diagnoses were greater in the children with comorbid ADHD+BPSD.
Children with comorbid BPSD+ADHD have more impaired global functioning than those with either diagnosis alone.
Teacher ratings of both ADHD and BPSD symptoms were more severe for comorbid ADHD+BPSD than BPSD alone, but not than ADHD alone.
Children with comorbid bipolar spectrum disorder (BPSD) + ADHD showed younger age of onset of BPSD symptoms than those with BPSD alone.

correct_answer.text: Children with comorbid bipolar spectrum disorder (BPSD) + ADHD showed younger age of onset of BPSD symptoms than those with BPSD alone.

correct_answers.text: Children with comorbid bipolar spectrum disorder (BPSD) + ADHD showed younger age of onset of BPSD symptoms than those with BPSD alone.

questions.explanation: The authors found that children with BPSD+ADHD had onset of mood symptoms at 6.7 years and those with BPSD alone had onset at 6.9 years (p = 0.8). However, they found the age of their first visit to the LAMS-site clinic was statistically significantly younger (9.6 vs. 10.5 years, p < 0.01).

questions.question_text: According to the 'Four-Year Longitudinal Course of Children and Adolescents with Bipolar Spectrum Disorders: The Course and Outcome of Bipolar Youth (COBY) Study' (B. Birmaher et al. 2009), during syndromal periods, compared to those with bipolar I disorder or bipolar disorder not otherwise specified (bipolar NOS), youth with bipolar II disorder spent more time experiencing which of the following symptoms?

correct_answer.text: Major depression

correct_answers.text: Major depression

questions.explanation: According to the study, during syndromal periods, youth with bipolar II disorder manifest with less frequent manic symptoms. Instead, they are more likely to present with major depression.

questions.question_text: According to the 'Four-Year Longitudinal Course of Children and Adolescents with Bipolar Spectrum Disorders: The Course and Outcome of Bipolar Youth (COBY) Study' (B. Birmaher et al. 2009), which of the following pairs of numbers reflects conversion rates of bipolar II to bipolar I and bipolar NOS to either bipolar I or bipolar II respectively?
questions.explanation: According to the study, 25% of youth with bipolar II converted to bipolar I, whereas 38% of those with bipolar disorder, NOS, converted to either bipolar I or II.

questions.question_text: According to 'Switching to Another SSRI or to Venlafaxine With or Without Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Adolescents With SSRI-Resistant Depression: The TORDIA Randomized Controlled Trial' (D. Brent et al. 2008), all of the following statements reflect the findings except:

options.text: Cognitive behavioral therapy plus a switch to another SSRI showed a higher response rate than a medication switch alone.
The response rate of venlafaxine is statistically significantly lower than that of a second SSRI.
Cognitive behavioral therapy plus a switch to venlafaxine showed a higher response rate than a medication switch alone.
A greater increase in diastolic blood pressure and pulse was found more frequently during venlafaxine treatment than during SSRI treatment.
No differential treatment effects on change in the CDRS-R, self-rated depressive symptoms, suicidal ideation, or the rate of harm-related or any other adverse events were found.

correct_answer.text: The response rate of venlafaxine is statistically significantly lower than that of a second SSRI.

correct_answers.text: The response rate of venlafaxine is statistically significantly lower than that of a second SSRI.

questions.explanation: According to the study, cognitive behavioral therapy plus a switch to a medication regimen (either venlafaxine or another SSRI) showed a higher response rate than a medication switch alone.

questions.question_text: According to 'Treatment of Resistant Depression in Adolescents (TORDIA): Week 24 Outcomes' (G. Emslie et al. 2010), out of 334 adolescents enrolled in the study, approximately which percent of youth achieved remission by 24 weeks?
questions.explanation: According to the study, out of 334 adolescents enrolled in the study, 38.9% achieved remission by 24 weeks. Initial treatment assignment did not affect treatment remission rates.

questions.question_text: According to 'Long-Term Outcome of Adolescent Depression Initially Resistant to SSRI Treatment' (B. Vitiello et al. 2011), the depressive symptom trajectory of the remitters diverged from that of non-remitters by the end of which of the following weeks of treatment?

correct_answer.text: Six weeks

correct_answers.text: Six weeks

questions.explanation: According to the study, the depressive symptom trajectory of remitters diverged from that of non-remitters by the first six weeks of treatment. They also found that by 72 weeks, approximately 60% of the randomized youth had reached remission, but one-fourth of remitted youth experienced a relapse.

questions.question_text: According to 'Treatment of Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor–Resistant Depression in Adolescents: Predictors and Moderators of Treatment Response' (J. R. Asarnow et al. 2009), all of the following are predictors of poorer treatment response except:

options.text: More months of preenrollment SSRI medication treatment
Higher baseline levels of suicidal ideation and hopelessness

correct_answer.text: More months of preenrollment SSRI medication treatment

correct_answers.text: More months of preenrollment SSRI medication treatment

questions.explanation: According to the study, 'fewer months' of preenrollment SSRI medication treatment is one of the poor response predictors among the others listed in the answers.

questions.question_text: A. B. Klomek et al. (2007) studied the relationships of 'Bullying, Depression, and Suicidality in Adolescents.' They found approximately 9% of the sample (2,342 9th through 12th grade students) reported being victimized frequently and 13% reported bullying others frequently. All of the following statements reflect their findings except:

options.text: Compared to boys who never bullied others, boys who frequently bullied others were more likely to commit suicide.
Compared to girls who never bullied others, girls who bullied (either frequently or infrequently) others were more likely to be depressed, to have SSI, and to attempt suicide.
Bullying was more prevalent in the school setting than away from school settings.
Compared to girls who were never victimized, victimized (either frequently or infrequently) girls were more likely to be depressed, to have SSI, and to attempt suicide.
Compared to boys who were never victimized, frequently victimized boys were more likely to be depressed, to have serious suicidal ideation (SSI), and to attempt suicide.

correct_answer.text: Compared to boys who never bullied others, boys who frequently bullied others were more likely to commit suicide.

correct_answers.text: Compared to boys who never bullied others, boys who frequently bullied others were more likely to commit suicide.

questions.explanation: Compared to boys who never bullied others, boys who frequently bullied others were not more likely to commit suicide, but were more likely to be depressed and to have SSI.

questions.question_text: Match definition of treatment outcome of depression to the description:

options.text: Emergence of symptoms of depression during the period of recovery (a new episode)
Absence of significant symptoms of depression (e.g., no more than one to two)
A DSM episode of depression during the period of remission
A period of at least two weeks and less than two months with no or very few depressive symptoms
No symptoms or a significant reduction in depressive symptoms for at least two weeks

correct_answer.text: No symptoms or a significant reduction in depressive symptoms for at least two weeks

correct_answers.text: No symptoms or a significant reduction in depressive symptoms for at least two weeks

questions.explanation: In general three phases are involved in the treatment of depression: acute, continuation, and maintenance, with a primary goal of achieving response and ultimately full remission during the acute phase. The goal of the continuation phase is to solidify the response to treatment and avoid relapses, whereas the goal of the maintenance phase is to prevent recurrence or new episodes. (Ref. 1, pp. 267–268)
